# Generated host: route facades

`facade-emitter.mjs` writes one thin `src/app` route file per route (#203). A facade imports only
from a fixed specifier (a package subpath such as `@nextsparkjs/core/...` or a project alias such as
`@/templates/...`), re-exports what Next.js reads at runtime, and re-declares as literals the segment
config Next.js reads statically:

```ts
// Generated by NextSpark from @/templates/blog/[slug]/page. Do not edit: regenerated on every build.
export { default } from "@/templates/blog/[slug]/page"
export { generateMetadata, generateStaticParams } from "@/templates/blog/[slug]/page"
export const revalidate = 60
```

```js
import { emitFacade, FacadeEmitError } from './facade-emitter.mjs'

const { target, content } = await emitFacade({
  kind: 'page',                           // a row of the table below
  target: 'blog/[slug]/page.tsx',         // relative to src/app
  specifier: '@/templates/blog/[slug]/page',
  file: '/abs/project/templates/blog/[slug]/page.tsx',
  projectRoot: '/abs/project',
  cacheComponents: false,                 // the host's next.config value (checked when given)
})
```

Every problem is a `FacadeEmitError` carrying all diagnostics (`code`, `file`, `line`, `exportName`,
`message`); nothing is dropped silently.

## Export table (Next.js 16.3.5)

Source of truth: `next-route-exports.json`. The tests fail when the installed Next.js version differs,
when Next's `AppSegmentConfigSchemaKeys` or `HTTP_METHODS` change, and when this rendering is stale.

| Kind | File | Default | Re-exported | Literal segment config | Facade directive |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| page | `page` | required | `generateMetadata`, `metadata`, `generateViewport`, `viewport`, `generateStaticParams` | `revalidate`, `dynamicParams`, `dynamic`, `fetchCache`, `instant`, `prefetch`, `unstable_dynamicStaleTime`, `preferredRegion`, `runtime`, `maxDuration`, `config` | - |
| layout | `layout` | required | `generateMetadata`, `metadata`, `generateViewport`, `viewport`, `generateStaticParams` | `revalidate`, `dynamicParams`, `dynamic`, `fetchCache`, `instant`, `prefetch`, `preferredRegion`, `runtime`, `maxDuration` | - |
| template | `template` | required | - | - | - |
| loading | `loading` | required | - | - | - |
| error | `error` | required | - | - | 'use client' (source must be client) |
| global-error | `global-error` | required | - | - | 'use client' (source must be client) |
| not-found | `not-found` | required | - | - | - |
| global-not-found | `global-not-found` | required | `metadata`, `generateMetadata` | - | - |
| forbidden | `forbidden` | required | - | - | - |
| unauthorized | `unauthorized` | required | - | - | - |
| default | `default` | required | - | - | - |
| route | `route` | forbidden | `GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`, `generateStaticParams` | `revalidate`, `dynamicParams`, `dynamic`, `fetchCache`, `preferredRegion`, `runtime`, `maxDuration`, `config` | - |
| sitemap | `sitemap` | required | `generateSitemaps` | `revalidate`, `dynamic`, `fetchCache`, `preferredRegion`, `runtime`, `maxDuration` | - |
| robots | `robots` | required | - | `revalidate`, `dynamic`, `fetchCache`, `preferredRegion`, `runtime`, `maxDuration` | - |
| manifest | `manifest` | required | - | `revalidate`, `dynamic`, `fetchCache`, `preferredRegion`, `runtime`, `maxDuration` | - |
| icon | `icon`, `icon0`-`icon9` | required | `generateImageMetadata`, `size`, `contentType` | `revalidate`, `dynamic`, `fetchCache`, `preferredRegion`, `runtime`, `maxDuration` | - |
| apple-icon | `apple-icon`, `apple-icon0`-`apple-icon9` | required | `generateImageMetadata`, `size`, `contentType` | `revalidate`, `dynamic`, `fetchCache`, `preferredRegion`, `runtime`, `maxDuration` | - |
| opengraph-image | `opengraph-image`, `opengraph-image0`-`opengraph-image9` | required | `generateImageMetadata`, `size`, `contentType`, `alt` | `revalidate`, `dynamic`, `fetchCache`, `preferredRegion`, `runtime`, `maxDuration` | - |
| twitter-image | `twitter-image`, `twitter-image0`-`twitter-image9` | required | `generateImageMetadata`, `size`, `contentType`, `alt` | `revalidate`, `dynamic`, `fetchCache`, `preferredRegion`, `runtime`, `maxDuration` | - |

Emitted forms: **default** `export { default } from '<source>'`; **re-exported** `export { name } from
'<source>'` (never through `export *`, which Next does not see); **literal** `export const name = <literal>`
copied from the source.

Next detects `generateStaticParams`, `generateSitemaps` and `generateImageMetadata` statically through
`specifier.orig`, so a source that exports one under an alias (`export { listSlugs as generateStaticParams }`,
which Next does *not* detect statically) is forwarded keeping that local name, and the facade reads the same:

```ts
import { generateStaticParams as listSlugs } from "@/templates/x/[slug]/page"
export { listSlugs as generateStaticParams }
```

Metadata image kinds accept Next's one-digit variants (`icon1`, `apple-icon9`, `opengraph-image2`,
`twitter-image3`), mapped to the base kind.

The emitter resolves `next/package.json` once (project first, then core) and accepts only `~16.3.5`: the table's
`next` is the verified baseline, and any stable 16.3.x patch at or above it is accepted, while other minors/majors,
lower patches and prereleases are refused (`NS_HOST_UNSUPPORTED_NEXT_VERSION`). It loads Next's segment config
schema from that same package root.
Every emitted facade is also validated by `static-imports.mjs` against an allowed grammar: a `'use client'`
prologue, static imports, `export { … } from '<string>'`, `export { … }` of imported names, and
`export const name = <literal Next reads>`. Nothing else - no expression, call, member access, function, class or
`export *` - so no runtime selection of a module can be written in a facade at all. Generated registries use the
`registry` grammar: static imports plus `export const X = <object/array literal>` whose leaves are literals or imported
identifiers (no computed keys, spreads, methods, getters or calls).

Segment config and `cacheComponents` (verified by probe builds with `next build --webpack` and
`--turbopack`, Next.js 16.3.5):

- invalid with `cacheComponents: true` (build error "Route segment config "X" is not compatible with
  `nextConfig.cacheComponents`"): `dynamic`, `dynamicParams`, `fetchCache`, `revalidate`, **`runtime`**
  (not listed in Next's docs, but even `runtime = 'nodejs'` fails);
- require `cacheComponents: true`: `instant`, `prefetch`;
- `unstable_dynamicStaleTime` is page-only (a layout fails the build).

Literal values are accepted exactly as `next/dist/build/analysis/extract-const-value.js` reads them
(no negative numbers, no parentheses, no identifiers) and then validated with Next's own
`parseAppSegmentConfig`.

## Diagnostics

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `NS_HOST_NON_LITERAL_SEGMENT_CONFIG` | segment config exported as anything but `export const x = <literal>` |
| `NS_HOST_INVALID_SEGMENT_CONFIG_VALUE` | a literal Next's schema rejects |
| `NS_HOST_CACHE_COMPONENTS_CONFLICT` | a key the host's `cacheComponents` setting makes Next reject |
| `NS_HOST_CLIENT_SERVER_ONLY_EXPORT` | metadata family, `generateStaticParams` or segment config from a `'use client'` module; a route/metadata route source marked `'use client'` |
| `NS_HOST_CLIENT_REQUIRED` | `error` / `global-error` source without `'use client'` |
| `NS_HOST_ROUTE_DEFAULT_EXPORT` | a Route Handler source with a default export |
| `NS_HOST_ROUTE_NO_METHODS` | a Route Handler source without HTTP methods |
| `NS_HOST_MISSING_DEFAULT` | a component or metadata file source without a default export |
| `NS_HOST_UNSUPPORTED_EXPORT` | any export the table does not list for the kind |
| `NS_HOST_UNCLASSIFIABLE_EXPORT` | `export *`, destructuring exports, `enum`, `namespace`, `export =` |
| `NS_HOST_SERVER_ACTIONS_MODULE` | a `'use server'` module used as a route file |
| `NS_HOST_PARSE_ERROR` | the source does not parse |
| `NS_HOST_UNSUPPORTED_NEXT_VERSION` | the project resolves a Next.js outside `~<table next>` (other minor/major, lower patch, prerelease), or it lacks the segment config schema |
| `NS_HOST_VARIABLE_LOOKUP` | an emitted facade leaves the allowed facade grammar (internal guard, `static-imports.mjs`) |
| `NS_HOST_TARGET_MISMATCH` / `NS_HOST_INVALID_SPECIFIER` / `NS_HOST_UNKNOWN_KIND` | bad emitter input |

## `nextspark prepare`: the whole generated host

The emitter writes one file; `prepare.mjs` generates the complete `src/app` and the registries of a project and
publishes them safely. The CLI runs `prepare-cli.mjs` from the installed core (`prepare`, `prepare --check`,
`build`, `dev`).

| Module | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `core-routes.mjs` | `loadCoreRouteManifest()`: the one loader of core's route manifest, resolved through the core package's `exports` (`@nextsparkjs/core/routes/manifest.json` -> `dist/routes/manifest.json` in the npm package; in a source checkout `src/routes/manifest.json` wins, since dist is its build output); `[{ kind, target, specifier, protected? }]`. Route modules resolve the same way (`./routes/*`). `routes/variants.json` (`{ "cacheComponents": [...] }`) replaces entries by target when the host's `cacheComponents` is on (read from a literal in `next.config.*`; unknown keeps the manifest entries). No manifest: the core cannot generate the host and prepare keeps the legacy registry build. Protected targets: `protected: true` or core's `PROTECTED_PATHS` (any level: a whole-file override cannot keep part of a route protected). |
| `mode.mjs` | `resolveHostMode()`: `host` when the core ships the manifest and `src/app` is absent, holds only empty directories and placeholders (`.gitkeep`, `README.md`, OS files - never touched), or is described by a valid generation record (parses, schema version, NextSpark paths only); `legacy-app` when `src/app` holds files and there is no valid record: the legacy registry build, silently (no command converts a committed src/app yet); `prepare --check` reports legacy mode, never fresh; `no-manifest` otherwise. Read-only. |
| `plan.mjs` | `planHost()`: core < plugin (`plugins/<name>/templates/**`, `plugins/<name>/api/**` at `api/plugins/<name>/**`) < project (`templates/**`, `api/**` at `api/**`). A higher layer replaces a lower one at the same directory + file stem (+ cache-mode suffix); two files of one layer, two plugins, anything over a protected core route, and a page with a Route Handler in one directory are diagnostics naming both sources. Sorted by code unit, so deterministic. |
| `render.mjs` | One facade per planned route through `emitFacade` (every cache mode the host builds is checked; a problem all modes share is reported once). Facade cache for the watcher. |
| `generation.mjs` | Ownership, validation, publication, lock and check (below). |
| `prepare.mjs` | `prepareHost()` / `checkHost()` / `watchHost()` for any host config; `projectHostConfig()` for a real project (the registry build runs into a staging directory: `NEXTSPARK_REGISTRIES_OUT`, `NEXTSPARK_GENERATED_HOST=1`, and its wall-clock timestamps are normalized so the same sources give the same bytes). |

Publication (`generation.mjs`):

- everything is planned, emitted, staged and validated (facade grammar for `src/app`, registry grammar where the producer
  declares it, paths only under `src/app` and `.nextspark/registries`) before the first write; a failure leaves the previous
  generation untouched;
- changed files are written to a temporary file beside them and renamed; unchanged files are not touched;
- `.nextspark/generation.json` records schema version, mode, core/cli/next versions, the hash of every input and every
  emitted file. It is written ahead (previous + new files, `pending: true`) and then final, so an interrupted run never leaves
  a file no record owns;
- ownership is proven against the disk: a `src/app` file is NextSpark's only when the previous record lists it **and** its
  bytes still have the recorded hash (for an interrupted publication, also the hash it had before). A listed file edited
  since, or a leftover record next to a tree that replaced the generated one, is foreign: never overwritten or deleted;
- only files of the previous record are deleted; nothing is written, replaced or deleted through a symlink (a symlink in or
  on the way to `src/app` or the registries stops the run; safe-fs refuses it too);
- `src/app` files that are not provably NextSpark's stop the run before it writes, naming them; an unowned file
  byte-identical to its generated content is adopted; placeholders (`.gitkeep`, `README.md`, OS files) are ignored;
- a file already in place of a generated registry that the previous record does not own is taken over only when a
  NextSpark registry build wrote it (byte-identical, or stamped `Generated at: <ISO time>` / `// Generated by NextSpark` in
  its first 30 lines, which every legacy registry carries); anything else stops the run (`NS_HOST_FOREIGN_REGISTRY`) and is
  left untouched;
- one writer at a time: `.nextspark/generation.lock`, only ever created with O_EXCL. A stale lock (its process gone on
  this machine; from another machine, older than 10 minutes; unreadable for more than 30 seconds) is never deleted and
  re-created: the one process that creates `generation.lock.takeover-<inode-mtime>` with O_EXCL re-checks the lock is
  still that instance and renames its own claim over it atomically. A live holder on this machine is never taken over.

`prepare --check` writes nothing and targets the production host (what `prepare` and `build` write): a `nextspark dev`
generation is reported as such; `--check --dev` checks it instead. `src/app` is re-rendered in memory and compared byte for
byte (missing / stale / foreign); a publication that did not finish (`pending`) is not fresh;
registries are compared with their recorded hashes and inputs with their recorded hashes (the registry build is not
side-effect free, so it is not re-run); no `src/app` and no record: "run nextspark prepare".

`nextspark dev`: the first generation must succeed before Next starts; `watchHost` then regenerates on changes under
`templates/`, `api/`, `plugins/`, `entities/`, `config/`, `blocks/`, `messages/`, `nextspark.config.ts`, core's route manifest
and packaged plugin manifests. A failed regeneration keeps the last valid host published **and served** (routes keep answering 200), prints the
diagnostic, and shows it in the browser without pretending the change was applied. What stays is `src/app`: the route
files, the names they forward and the segment config copied as literals. Edits inside modules the existing facades import
still reach Next directly (a facade re-exports the module, it does not copy it), so the message says exactly that:

- a dev generation adds three fixed files under `src/app/_nextspark/` (a private folder, never routes):
  `generation-diagnostic.ts` (`export const generationDiagnostic = ""`), `generation-status-reporter.tsx` (a `'use client'`
  component that, while the diagnostic is non-empty, shows it in a fixed dev panel and calls `console.error` once, which Next's
  dev indicator lists as an issue; the panel is what stays reliable, since Next clears its issue list on every Fast Refresh
  rebuild) and `generation-status.tsx`
  (`withGenerationStatus(Layout)`, the root layout with the reporter rendered before its children);
- the dev root layout facade is `export default withGenerationStatus(Source)` (`dev-facade` grammar);
- on failure the watcher rewrites only `generation-diagnostic.ts`; Next's HMR re-renders and the reporter shows the
  diagnostic. The next successful regeneration empties it and the panel goes away, with no reload.

A production preparation never emits these files or the composition: zero bytes and zero code in production builds.

Tests: `node --test packages/core/scripts/build/registry/host/__tests__/*.test.mjs`.
